title: WF03 OIDC-27..34 residual aggregate blocker: OIDC-11 integration tenant fixture collisions caused RealmOwnershipMismatch under parallel aggregate runs
summary: Resolved the remaining aggregate integration blocker by isolating OIDC-11 integration fixtures per test and hardening tenant cleanup. The previous shared tenant fixture allowed realm-binding collisions across aggregate runs, surfacing intermittent RealmOwnershipMismatch in createOrGetJitOidcUser.

root_cause.details: OIDC-11 integration cases reused one tenant identifier and one tenant slug while each case bound a different realm. Under aggregate execution this created cross-test fixture interference and stale tenant state collisions, so realm ownership checks failed nondeterministically.

changes: Assigned per-test tenant UUIDs/slugs for OIDC-11 integration cases that provision users.
Added cleanupTenantFixture helper to remove tenant-scoped dependent rows and delete tenant records by id, slug, and realm before/after each fixture-bound test.
Kept service-layer realm-ownership logic unchanged; fix remained test-scoped and targeted.

prevention: Do not share mutable tenant fixtures across integration tests that bind different realms.
For tenant-bound identity tests, clean dependent user rows and tenant rows by id plus alternate unique keys before re-binding.
Prefer per-test fixture identifiers in aggregate suites where Zig can schedule tests in parallel.
